trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), walked with next_token(), gated ordinary text on get_token_type() === '#text', and explicitly opted into TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text with !is_tag_closer(). All HTML API calls are documented in the rendered files and execution recorded no _doing_it_wrong notices. Edge handling matches the docs: decoded get_modifiable_text(), raw SCRIPT/STYLE excluded, null processor handled, and UTF-8 truncation used.

Correct processor and documented APIs throughout. The text policy is right: #text plus explicit TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text, excluding SCRIPT/STYLE. Slightly less idiomatic than trial-1 because it calls is_tag_closer()/get_token_name() on non-text tokens without first checking get_token_type() === '#tag', but the documented return semantics make this harmless here. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Correctly uses WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_token(), get_token_type(), get_token_name(), is_tag_closer(), and get_modifiable_text(); all are documented. The implementation is compact and follows the special-element opt-in rule. Minor idiom deduction for testing get_token_name() before confirming a tag token and for relying directly on mb_substr(), but there is no undocumented HTML API usage or runtime misuse.

failure_analysis: All three trials passed all 10 hidden cases, so there are no failed hidden cases to attribute to documentation gaps. The docs did well on the exact hard parts of this task: the HTML Processor overview says to choose WP_HTML_Processor when structure matters and when collecting element text; create_fragment() is documented as the BODY-fragment factory; next_token() explains that text can be split across multiple #text tokens and that SCRIPT/STYLE/TITLE/TEXTAREA carry no #text children; get_modifiable_text() clearly says #text, TITLE, and TEXTAREA are decoded UTF-8, while SCRIPT/STYLE are raw; and the text-extraction recipe warns not to treat every token with modifiable text as ordinary DOM text. Near-misses were small: trials 2 and 3 leaned on get_token_name()/is_tag_closer() behavior for non-tag tokens instead of first checking #tag, and none checked paused_at_incomplete_token() or get_last_error(); however the docs explicitly leave read-only incomplete-input policy to the caller, and the task did not require rejecting partial scans.

doc_gaps.problem: The examples show tag-only use, but the return contract for non-tag tokens is implicit. Trial code safely relied on false for non-tags, but a reader has to infer that from implementation or from broader token docs.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add one sentence: when not matched on a tag token, this method returns false; callers that need an opening element should prefer get_token_type() === '#tag' && ! is_tag_closer().

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain ordinary subtree text and named special-element text separately. This task required a combined policy: all ordinary body text plus selected decoded special elements, excluding raw special elements. The subjects inferred it correctly, but the distinction is subtle.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short general example or policy note showing how to combine ordinary #text collection with an explicit whitelist of decoded special-element opener text, while leaving SCRIPT/STYLE raw text out unless specifically requested.
